text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Rice exports in the first 10-1/2 months of this year were 2.75 million tonnes and the total for the whole year may reach 3.0 million.
-- The economy bounced back in October and November and gross domestic product (GDP) growth is expected to be 9.5 percent for the whole of 1996.

-- The sugar industry has pledged to produce enough sugar to meet estimated domestic demand of 300,000 tonnes in 1997, one step in the state-supported goal of producing one million tonnes of sugar by 2000.
-- Fuel prices have been increased for the third time this year and the price of electricity has been raised by 12.6 percent.
-- The central State Bank of Vietnam has issued urgent measures to ensure the quality of credit and overdue debt collection.
-- Vietnam has 180,000 drug addicts, ranking second among ASEAN countries after the Phillipines for the number of addicts.
-- The Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam has raised its saving interest rates.
-- Vietnam expects $2 billion to be pledged by foreign donors during a two-day World Bank Consultative Group meeting later this week.
